description: A user can align any paragraph of the cover letter's opening, body and closing fields left, center, right or justified, as in Microsoft Word, and every place the letter appears shows that alignment. The banner shown when a letter is created from a job application reads in the user's interface language.

userStories.title: A letter's paragraphs can be aligned left, center, right or justified
userStories.description: As a user editing a cover letter, I want to align a paragraph of my opening, body or closing as I would in Word, so that the letter is laid out the way I want.
acceptanceCriteria: The toolbar of the opening paragraph, of every body paragraph (including one added with "add paragraph"), and of the closing paragraph shows four alignment buttons: left, center, right and justify, in that order.

Clicking a button aligns the paragraph that holds the cursor. With a selection spanning several paragraphs of the same field, it aligns each of them. Other paragraphs in the field keep their alignment.

The button for the alignment of the paragraph holding the cursor is shown as active, and moves when the cursor moves to a paragraph aligned differently. A paragraph with no alignment set shows left as active.
Each button has an accessible name and a tooltip in the interface language (fr, en, de, it), reachable and operable with the keyboard, with visible focus.
The alignment is saved with the letter and is still there after a reload.
Both previews (the editor pane and the preview window) show each paragraph with its alignment.
The downloaded PDF shows each paragraph with its alignment.
The downloaded Word file gives each paragraph the matching Word alignment: left, centered, right or justified.
A letter whose paragraphs have no alignment set looks the same as today in the editor, both previews, the PDF and the Word file: left-aligned.
The CV's rich-text fields show no new button.

FR-1: Alignment is a property of a paragraph inside the field's existing rich-text HTML, as `text-align` with one of `left`, `center`, `right` or `justify`. Nothing new is stored and there is no separate setting.
FR-2: The editor, both previews, the PDF and the Word file all read the alignment from that same stored HTML (CLAUDE.md §10). There is no second source.
FR-3: The sanitizer allows no new style property or value. Any alignment value outside the four is dropped or treated as left.
FR-4: The alignment controls appear only on the cover letter's opening, body and closing fields.
FR-5: Every new user-facing string comes from the existing i18n dictionaries in fr, en, de and it.

Regression constraint: The CV editor's ribbon, key-achievements toolbar and every CV field behave and look as before. `pnpm test:parity` and `pnpm test:visual` keep their current results: MATCH 211 / KNOWN 3 / NEW 0, and 10/10.
Regression constraint: The letter's existing formatting buttons (bold, italic, underline, lists, font, size) behave as before in the three fields.
Regression constraint: A stored letter without alignment produces the same PDF and Word output as before.
Regression constraint: The page-break marker and the one-page check (`cover-letter-one-page`) behave as before. Alignment never changes how many lines a paragraph takes.
Regression constraint: The banner's second line, and the rest of the "new letter" page, are unchanged.
Verification: Unit tests for the alignment command on the letter's fields: setting each of the four values, a multi-paragraph selection, and the active state.
Verification: Unit tests showing that the stored HTML keeps each of the four values through sanitizing, and drops any other value.
Verification: An e2e test: align paragraphs in the opening, body and closing differently, save, reload, then check the editor, the preview window and the downloaded PDF.

Verification: Export validation: a letter with one paragraph per alignment, downloaded as PDF and Word. In the PDF, check each paragraph's position on the page. In the Word file, check each paragraph's `w:jc`.

Verification: Browser evidence (e2e plus screenshots) of the toolbar in the editor pane at the widths the editor already supports, in fr, en, de and it, and of the banner on `/fr`, `/en`, `/de` and `/it`.
Verification: `ui-expert` validation of the buttons next to the existing ribbon and the CV's key-achievements toolbar, and of the banner.
Verification: The CLAUDE.md §14 baseline, with lint at or below the tracked ceiling. Also `pnpm test:parity` and `pnpm test:visual`.
FAIL condition: Missing control: a button is missing in any of the three fields, including a newly added body paragraph.
FAIL condition: Wrong scope: a button aligns a whole field or another paragraph, contrary to the owner's per-paragraph decision.
FAIL condition: Lost alignment: the editor, a preview, the PDF or the Word file shows a paragraph with a different alignment from the one stored.
FAIL condition: Output change: a letter without alignment looks different from before in any of those places.
FAIL condition: CV change: an alignment button appears on a CV field, or the CV ribbon changes.
FAIL condition: Hard-coded or wrong text: a button label or the banner title is hard-coded, or appears in English on `/fr`, `/de` or `/it`.
FAIL condition: Weaker sanitizer: the sanitizer allows a new style property or value.
BLOCKER condition: The editor's alignment command cannot produce `text-align` on a paragraph in a form the existing sanitizer keeps without widening it. If so, the method must go back to the owner.
Out of scope: Any alignment control on the CV's fields, or any change to the CV's ribbon or key-achievements toolbar.
Out of scope: The greeting, sign-off, sender, recipient, subject, date and annexes fields: they are not rich text.
Out of scope: Keyboard shortcuts for alignment.
Out of scope: Line spacing, indentation, or any other Word paragraph option.
Out of scope: The tools-page cover-letter generator, the letter checker, and the AI's output: an AI letter is created left-aligned, as today.
Out of scope: Translation (`/api/cover-letters/[id]/translate`): it is not changed. Its effect on alignment is recorded under Risks.
Out of scope: The banner's layout, colour and second line. The CV's "new" page and its banner.
Out of scope: Any database change.

userStories.title: The banner for a letter created from a job application is in the user's language
userStories.description: As a user creating a cover letter from a job-application card, I want the banner above the form in my interface language, so that the page does not switch to English.
acceptanceCriteria: On `/fr`, `/en`, `/de` and `/it`, the banner title on `/dashboard/cover-letters/new?jobApplicationId=…` is a cover-letter wording in that locale, from the dictionaries. It does not show the English fallback outside `/en`.
The banner's second line is unchanged: the job title, the translated "at" word, and the company.
The CV's banner (`resumes.new.creatingForJob`) is unchanged.
